chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who says regarding a believer what his eyes saw and his ears heard, so he is from those for whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:
Indeed, those who like that immorality should spread among those who believe, for them is a painful punishment.

key_terms.مَنْ: Who (indefinite pronoun used for general ruling)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of backbiting a believer based on personal observation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi emphasizes the severity of backbiting by equating the act of reporting witnessed faults with the Quranic concept of 'shai'ah' (spreading scandal), thereby linking personal observation to communal spiritual harm. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that exposing a believer's private sins, even if true, constitutes a grave sin that invites 'adhab alim' (painful punishment), serving as a deterrent against namimah (slander).
